source.annotation: Isolates an executable prompt override instruction without executing any command.
Ordinary user-facing prompt prose asks for confirmation and does not override policy.
Uses a clearly synthetic hardcoded API key-shaped value for static detection only.
Generates a process-local token at runtime rather than embedding a credential in source.
A skill declares browser access even though the fixture has no browser capability.
The skill declares only read access to its own package files and no broad permissions.
The dependency uses a wildcard version and is intentionally not reproducibly locked.
The dependency uses an exact version and a neutral package name with no registry override.
The scan deliberately omits acquisition commit provenance while retaining a complete content hash.
The same source-integrity rule receives a valid acquired commit and complete scan input.
A local companion opens an explicitly constructed localhost URL with execFile and no shell.
A test harness starts a fixed local server with an argv array and shell explicitly disabled.
Documentation demonstrates code that package authors must recognize as unsafe; the fixture never executes it.
Cleanup is statically confined beneath the package directory and only removes disposable session state.
The token is freshly generated from a cryptographic random source and is not a third-party credential.
The URL-shaped string is constructed only for an equality check and is never used as a network destination.
The server binds only to the loopback interface and exposes no remote network surface.
A fixed HTTPS image URL is presentation content, not a dependency registry or executable download.
An HTTP query parameter reaches a shell-capable child-process call without validation or authentication.
A remote attacker-controlled script is downloaded and immediately piped into a shell interpreter.
A GitHub credential is read from the operator environment and sent to an attacker-controlled endpoint.
An untrusted request path controls an unbounded recursive filesystem deletion operation.
The code opens a connection to the link-local cloud metadata address and requests IAM credentials.
A publicly bound HTTP service accepts a command parameter and invokes a shell without authentication.
An operator-supplied hook is shell-capable, but its safety depends on deployment ownership and policy.
The pair differs only in bind host; this variant is restricted to the local machine.
The pair differs only in bind host; this variant exposes the service beyond loopback.
The command comes from operator configuration rather than an unauthenticated request.
The command comes directly from an HTTP request query with no validation or authentication.
The Origin value is compared with configuration and never dereferenced as a URL.
The attacker-controlled Origin header is dereferenced as an outbound request destination.
The recursive deletion target is a fixed cache directory beneath the package itself.
The recursive deletion target is taken directly from an untrusted request parameter.
The value is a newly generated local session token and grants no third-party authority.
The value is a third-party GitHub credential whose legitimacy depends on declared purpose and scope.
Malformed manifest JSON is reported as an SR-010 finding without executing or loading package code.
Complete manifest metadata and the required skill document form the metadata near-miss.
A benign package includes a source-matched Python cache to pin the production structural policy.
Prints a token-shaped runtime value directly to stdout without an escaping boundary.
The value is passed through an escaping helper before output and does not match the unsafe sink pattern.
Reads a system prompt resource through a code-side file helper for deterministic static detection.
Mentions system prompt terminology in ordinary prose without a read, write, or network API.
Calls an explicit persistent-memory editing API, without invoking it during benchmark collection.
Writes a package-owned state file and does not target agent memory, context, or history.
Reads a shared .claude configuration path rather than information owned by the fixture itself.
Reads a package-owned state path and contains no cross-agent or shared configuration access.
Registers a code-side MCP tool that is absent from the declared manifest tool list.
Uses a remote plaintext MCP endpoint so transport protection is tested independently.
Describes deletion capability while declaring read-only filesystem permission, creating a deterministic contradiction.
Declares one read-only MCP tool over HTTPS with a matching filesystem permission.
A plugin lifecycle hook contains shell metacharacters instead of a declarative event name.
A plugin component path escapes its package directory through a parent traversal segment.
Uses a named lifecycle event and a package-local component path without shell syntax.
Runs a subagent autonomously for one hundred iterations without an approval boundary.
Keeps a subagent supervised, project-scoped, low-iteration, and limited to a read tool.
A package bin entry contains a recursive-removal pattern token for static installer review; it is not executable.
A nested package lifecycle script tests recursive discovery without inheriting parent files.
Contains no lifecycle script and no executable bin entry, so installation has no automatic action.
Uses an import alias and shell-enabled subprocess call to exercise the AST detector independently of regex.
